meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le accident', plural 'les accidents') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'mishap'.

examples.trans: It was an accident.

examples.text: Complètement par accident! Chez mon cousin, je l'ai ouverte et j'ai vu des partitions et un ruban rouge.
examples.trans: By complete accident! At my cousin's flat, I opened it and saw sheet music and a red ribbon.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Où est-ce que j'accroche ce miroir rond? À gauche de la fenêtre ou à droite?
examples.trans: Where should I hang this round mirror? Left of the window or right?
It is easy to hang up, hook together.

meanings.note: en tête d'affiche = top-billed, starring

examples.text: Guy Marchand est en tête d'affiche.
examples.trans: Guy Marchand has top billing.
A beautiful movie poster.

examples.text: C'est la nouvelle affiche de mon film.
examples.trans: It is the new poster for my movie.

meanings.note: In French pastry, *aux amandes* (plural) describes dishes made with ground or sliced almonds (*biscuits aux amandes*, *pâte aux amandes*).

examples.text: Elle prépare des biscuits dorés aux amandes pour le thé.
examples.trans: She bakes golden almond biscuits for tea.

examples.text: Un peu de poudre d'amande rend la pâte plus fondante.
examples.trans: A little almond flour makes the crust more tender.

meanings.note: for counting: vingt ans; for age: j'ai vingt ans

examples.trans: His twenty years of career.
She's forty.

meanings.note: Masculine or feminine. This lesson uses masculine cet après-midi. Both après-midi and après-midis are accepted plural spellings.

examples.trans: I'm working this afternoon.

examples.text: Je vous en prie, madame. Lundi après-midi, l'entrée était sombre.
examples.trans: Go right ahead, madam. Monday afternoon, the lobby was dark.

meanings.note: Architectural arch over a passage.

examples.text: Juste sous cette arche. Je vais monter la valise bleue pour vous.
examples.trans: Right under this archway. I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.
Here is the arch, archway on the table.

meanings.note: Time: avant mon départ.

examples.trans: Last meeting before I leave.
Come before noon.
You're having lunch with Audiard.
With pleasure!

meanings.note: avoir peur = to be afraid, avoir raison = to be right, avoir 40 ans = to be 40

meanings.en: helper verb of the passé composé
meanings.note: J'ai appelé = I called.

meanings.en: il y a = there is, there are
meanings.note: Fixed expression.

examples.trans: I've got a little loft.
You have a meeting.

baisser.gloss: to lower, to turn down; to go down

meanings.en: to lower, to drop (eyes, head, voice)
meanings.note: baisser les yeux = to lower one's eyes
les prix baissent = prices are falling

examples.trans: Turn the music down a bit.

examples.text: Laissez-moi baisser mes lunettes de mon front... Chambre neuf?!
examples.trans: Let me pull my glasses down from my forehead... Room nine?!

meanings.note: Park, courtyard, or stone bench.

examples.text: Asseyons-nous un instant sur le banc à l'ombre.
examples.trans: Let's sit for a moment on the bench in the shade.

examples.text: Un vieux banc en pierre fait face à la fontaine.
examples.trans: An old stone bench faces the fountain.

meanings.note: Très bien = very well, fine.
C'est bien.

examples.trans: Very well.
She's nice.

meanings.note: À bientôt = see you soon.

examples.trans: See you soon!
He's arriving soon.

meanings.note: Built from bouche ('mouth').

examples.text: Une bouchée... Antoine, ferme les yeux! Ça a exactement le même goût que le gâteau de grand-père!
examples.trans: One bite... Antoine, close your eyes! That tastes exactly like Grandfather's cake!

examples.text: Voici la bouchée sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the bite, mouthful on the table.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la bouilloire', plural 'les bouilloires') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'kettle'.

examples.trans: The electric kettle.

examples.text: J'ouvre le couvercle de la bouilloire.
examples.trans: I open the lid of the kettle.

meanings.note: Birch tree or its pale, smooth wood ('bois de bouleau').

examples.text: Ces pinces à linge sont taillées dans du bois de bouleau bien lisse.
examples.trans: These clothespins are carved from smooth birchwood.

examples.text: L'écorce blanche du bouleau brille au soleil d'automne.
examples.trans: The white bark of the birch tree gleams in the autumn sun.

meanings.note: determiner: ce soir = tonight, cette semaine = this week
pronoun: c'est = it is; tout ce que = all that

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
examples.trans: I can't come tonight.

examples.text: Il y a vingt-cinq ans? Dans cette même maison?
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago? In that same house?

meanings.note: Une chambre d'hôtel.
Une chambre d'hôtel.

examples.trans: A room at the Carlton.
She's in her room.

meanings.note: Invariable, singular noun.

examples.trans: Botox every year.
I work every day.

meanings.note: The final q is pronounced: sɛ̃k.

examples.trans: I can take off five years.
Five minutes.

examples.text: Regardez l'horloge: il est midi moins cinq!
examples.trans: Look at the clock: it is five to twelve!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le coin', plural 'les coins') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'corner'.

examples.trans: I need a quiet corner.

examples.text: Faites beaucoup de parts du coin, ma chère!
examples.trans: Make plenty of corner pieces, my dear!
In the courtyard.

examples.text: Seulement le tilleul de la cour et la pluie.
examples.trans: Only the linden tree in the courtyard and the rain.

meanings.note: Uphill slope; seacoast; rib ('côte à côte' = side by side).

examples.text: Ils marchent côte à côte le long des arbres.

examples.text: La petite rue monte en côte jusqu'à la tour.

meanings.note: D' before a vowel.

examples.trans: The Kechiche film.

meanings.note: The x sounds like z before a vowel.

examples.trans: Two tickets.
Twice.

meanings.note: past forms use être: elle est devenue

examples.trans: She became a star.

examples.text: Trop tard! Il a dit merci et il a raccroché!

meanings.note: pronounced dis alone, di before a consonant, diz before a vowel

for things you can't count; de la (feminine)

examples.trans: It's compost.

Object pronoun replacing a phrase introduced by de. The English wording depends on the expression: en parler means to talk about it; j'en ai assez means I have had enough.
Object pronoun referring to an unspecified amount or to a quantity named after the action: j'en ai deux means I have two (of them).

examples.trans: I'm late.
Are you on holiday?
We're talking about it.

meanings.note: je ne veux pas l'entendre = I don't want to hear it

examples.text: Très généreux! Vous avez entendu la cloche du portail en bas?

It is easy to wipe, dry together.

meanings.note: The t is never pronounced.

examples.trans: And you?
And tomorrow?

meanings.note: Fermer la porte.

examples.text: Excusez-moi, la porte est fermée à clé?
examples.trans: Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.trans: Stay here with all of you? Yes, a hundred times yes!

examples.trans: My bread is already in the oven, at least.

examples.text: Tout droit sorti du four: le gâteau au citron du vendredi, avec les parts du coin!
examples.trans: Straight out of the oven: Friday lemon cake, with the corner pieces!

meanings.note: For receiving income or a wage.
For winning a game, competition or prize.

examples.trans: What each person earns.
We won!

meanings.note: Garder un enfant.

examples.trans: Keep the change.

examples.trans: You carry a screwdriver everywhere on you, Henri!

examples.text: Chacun ses goûts, mais moi je préfère le café bien serré.
examples.trans: To each their own taste, though I prefer my coffee nice and strong.

meanings.en: to taste, try a bite or spoonful of
meanings.note: Direct object (goûter ce miel = 'taste this honey') or goûter à quelque chose. As a masculine noun, le goûter is the afternoon snack around 4 p.m.

examples.text: Goûtez une petite cuillère de ce miel doré!
examples.trans: Taste a little spoonful of this golden honey!

examples.text: Thibault goûte toujours la pâte avant d'enfourner.
examples.trans: Thibault always tastes the batter before putting it in the oven.

examples.trans: She's a big star.

meanings.note: Before the noun: un gros contrat.
About people: not polite.

examples.trans: It's a big problem.
A big contract.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le gâteau', plural 'les gâteaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cake'.

examples.trans: A cake with candy.
A chocolate cake.

examples.text: Onze heures vingt. Le gâteau est prêt, Nadia?
examples.trans: Eleven twenty. Is the cake ready, Nadia?

meanings.note: Used almost exclusively in the expression hocher la tête ('to nod one's head' in agreement or thought).
Begins with an aspirated h (le hochement, je hoche without elision).

examples.text: Puis il a hoché la tête deux fois vers Étienne et a écrit deux mots sur sa serviette: Même goût!
examples.trans: Then he nodded twice to Etienne and wrote two words on his napkin: Exact taste!

examples.text: Henri hoche la tête en écoutant le plan d'Antoine.
examples.trans: Henri nods his head while listening to Antoine's plan.
He is here.
There is a meeting.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem. Prefix 'im-' marks negation ('un-, im-') or inward motion.

examples.trans: Talk to Ramzy immediately.

examples.text: Je dois régler ce problème immédiatement.
examples.trans: I must settle this problem immediately.
Come immediately.

meanings.note: definite article; l' before a vowel
As a direct-object pronoun: le is masculine, la feminine; both become l' before a vowel sound.

examples.trans: The film is fantastic.
The Koltès play.

meanings.note: Months are masculine and never capitalised in French: en mai ('in May'), le dix mai ('on the tenth of May', using cardinal dix).

examples.text: Le tilleul de la cour commence à fleurir fin mai.
examples.trans: The linden tree in the courtyard begins to bloom in late May.

examples.text: La carte postale est datée du dix mai.
examples.trans: The postcard is dated the tenth of May.

meanings.en: a hand, help (un coup de main)

examples.trans: Wash your hands.

examples.text: Elle a un stylo à la main.
examples.trans: She has a pen in her hand.

meanings.note: La lune de miel = honeymoon. Masculine noun ('le miel', plural 'les miels') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sweet honey'.

examples.trans: Sweet honey.

examples.text: Voilà pour vous, madame: du thé chaud à la menthe et du miel.
examples.trans: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea and honey.

examples.text: Excellent choix! Vous voulez du miel ou de la confiture de pommes à côté?
examples.trans: Wonderful choice! Would you like honey or apple jam on the side?

meanings.note: Cinq minutes = five minutes.

examples.trans: Wait five minutes.
I'll be there in a minute.

meanings.note: en mode silencieux = on silent mode
À la mode. Masculine noun ('le mode', plural 'les modes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'mode'.

examples.trans: It was on silent mode.
Change the phone setting.

examples.text: Il était en mode silencieux. Tu veux une coupe? On a sorti le champagne.
examples.trans: It was on silent mode. Do you want a glass? We brought out the champagne.

meanings.note: Ma before a feminine noun; mon before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel sound or mute h.

examples.trans: I'm at my lesson.
It's my seat.

meanings.note: Note the silent final t.

examples.text: Je ne comprends pas un mot.
examples.trans: I don't understand a word.
Say a word to me.

meanings.note: From mouiller. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'wet'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: My feet are already wet!
The grass is wet.

examples.text: Parce que les volets en bois mouillés adoucissent l'écho des pavés...
examples.trans: Because wet wooden shutters soften the echo from the cobblestones...

meanings.note: Person who plays a musical instrument or composes music.
Feminine form: une musicienne.

examples.trans: You played like a true musician, Antoine, and look who is standing up at table number one!

examples.text: Voici six nouvelles parts pour la table trois; garde deux gros coins pour les musiciens!
examples.trans: Here go six more slices for table three; save two big corners for the musicians!

meanings.note: Jouer de la musique ('play music'), écouter de la musique ('listen to music'), de la musique écrite à la main ('handwritten music').

examples.trans: The piano music drifts gently across the courtyard.

examples.text: J'aime travailler le matin avec un peu de musique classique.
examples.trans: I like working in the morning with a bit of classical music.

meanings.en: to deserve, to merit, to be worth

examples.text: Il le mérite après huit ans!
examples.trans: He deserves it after eight years!
You deserve a holiday.

meanings.note: Before a noun, means the same; can take a plural s in this use.

It's the same thing.

examples.text: Il y a vingt-cinq ans? Dans cette même maison?
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago? In that same house?

meanings.note: Final f sounds like /v/ before ans and heures.
Un gilet neuf, une ampoule neuve.

meanings.note: une note de frais = an expense claim

Take notes.

examples.text: Toutes mes notes de la semaine sont dedans. Vous me sauvez.

We understand.
Come with us!

meanings.note: before the noun; nouvel before a vowel
Un nouveau caprice.

examples.text: Oh, ça s'ouvre! Merci. Je suis Claire, la nouvelle réceptionniste.
examples.trans: Oh, it opens! Thank you. I am Claire, the new receptionist.

meanings.note: From noix ('walnut'); en noyer or en bois de noyer describes fine dark-grained walnut furniture and pianos.

meanings.note: Fruit.

meanings.note: Faire une pause = to take a break. Feminine noun ('la pause', plural 'les pauses') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'break'.

meanings.note: Affectionate, a bit condescending.

examples.trans: I've got a little loft.

meanings.note: Jouer du piano = to play the piano.

examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago, I taught piano lessons near here.

meanings.note: Poser une question.

examples.text: Ce sont les petits pains du matin! Prends-en un pendant qu'il est chaud.
examples.trans: They are the morning rolls! Take one while it is warm.

examples.text: Quelqu'un à la gare a pris ma valise bleue par erreur!
examples.trans: Someone at the train station took my blue suitcase by mistake!

examples.text: Comme c'est étrange! Nous avons pris le même train ce matin pour le même quartier.
examples.trans: How strange! We rode the same train this morning to the same district.

meanings.note: Près de = near.

examples.text: Il y a vingt-cinq ans, je donnais des cours de piano près d'ici.
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago, I taught piano lessons near here.

examples.text: Dix, onze, douze. Le compte est bon au centime près, merci!
examples.trans: Ten, eleven, twelve. Exact to the last cent, thank you!

examples.text: À droite, près du bureau, là où la lumière est bonne.
examples.trans: On the right, near the desk, where the light is good.

meanings.note: Connects actions in sequence.

examples.trans: He works, then he goes home.

examples.text: Non, soulevez d'abord la poignée, puis poussez.
examples.trans: No, lift the handle first, then push.

meanings.note: Joins two parts: dis-lui que.
Relative: tout ce que.
With ne: ne... que.
Ça fait trois semaines que.

examples.text: Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir.
examples.trans: Tell her I can't come.
I've only got two tickets.

meanings.note: qu'est-ce que tu racontes? = what are you talking about?

examples.trans: Tell me a story.

examples.text: Le film raconte la vie de ma mère.
examples.trans: The film tells the story of my mother's life.

examples.text: Nadia l'a préparé ce matin quand Madame Odette lui a raconté nos vendredis.
examples.trans: Nadia baked it this morning when Madam Odette told her about our Fridays.

meanings.note: Folded-back front edge (lapel) of a jacket or coat, or the reverse side of a page, medal, or hand.
Invariable in the plural: le revers, les revers.

examples.text: Et chaque voisin a accroché sa pince en bouleau numérotée sur le revers de sa veste!
examples.trans: And every neighbour clipped their numbered birch clothespin onto their jacket lapel!

examples.text: Étienne lisse le revers de sa veste avant d'ouvrir le portail.
examples.trans: Etienne smooths the lapel of his jacket before opening the gate.

meanings.note: Dans la rue = in the street.

examples.text: Nadia parle à tout le monde dans notre rue comme à de vieux amis.
examples.trans: Nadia talks to everyone on our street like old friends.

examples.text: Parfait. La fenêtre donne sur la rue ou sur la cour?
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street or the courtyard?

examples.text: Pas de numéro de téléphone, malheureusement. Seulement deux initiales et un vieux nom de rue.
examples.trans: No phone number, unfortunately. Only two initials and an old street name.

meanings.note: Reflexive verb.
Polite imperative.

examples.trans: Have a seat, please.
Sit there.

meanings.note: Means bath towel in a room and napkin at the table.

examples.text: Calmez-vous, Étienne. La chambre est propre et les serviettes sont fraîches.
examples.trans: Relax, Etienne. The room is clean and the towels are fresh.

examples.text: Où vont les petites cuillères et les serviettes?
examples.trans: Where do the small spoons and napkins go?

examples.text: Mets une serviette et une petite cuillère à côté de chaque tasse bleue.
examples.trans: Put one napkin and one teaspoon beside every blue cup.

meanings.note: pronounced si before a consonant: six jours = si ʒuʁ

examples.trans: Six months.

examples.text: Non, Étienne, le couple du sud est arrivé dans la chambre six il y a une heure.
examples.trans: No, Etienne, the couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.

related.word: pronounced si before a consonant: six jours

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun owned (son sac, sa valise, ses clés); used before feminine vowel-initial nouns too.
Masculine noun: le son du piano.

examples.trans: His twenty years of career.
It's her agent.

meanings.note: Sous la pluie = in the rain. Core French preposition meaning 'under', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Le chat dort sous la table.
examples.trans: The cat sleeps under the table.

examples.text: J'avais les mains froides sous le choc!
examples.trans: My hands were cold from the shock!

examples.text: Une chambre sous les toits? Je peux la voir d'abord?
examples.trans: An attic room? May I see it first?

meanings.note: A set of connected rooms in a hotel.
Very common.
La suite de l'histoire.

examples.trans: A suite at the Carlton.
I'm booking a suite.

meanings.note: Sur la table, sur la route.
Sur haut-parleur = on speaker.

examples.text: Le livre est sur la table.
examples.trans: The book is on the table.
You're on speaker.

meanings.note: A piece of furniture.
In à table, it is a call to come and eat, not a name for the meal itself.

examples.trans: Dinner's ready!

examples.text: Nous avons déjeuné à cette table.
examples.trans: We had lunch at this table.

examples.text: Il y a deux mois, lui et moi avons déjeuné à cette table.
examples.trans: Two months ago, he and I had lunch at this table.
Tea?
I'll have a tea.

meanings.note: Fragrant courtyard shade tree; also herbal tea.

examples.text: Sur la cour, juste au-dessus du vieux tilleul. C'est très calme.
examples.trans: The courtyard, right above the old linden tree. It is very quiet.

examples.text: Bienvenue à l'Hôtel du Tilleul, Claire. Votre deuxième jour ne sera pas ennuyeux.
examples.trans: Welcome to the Hotel du Tilleul, Claire. Your second day will not be boring.

examples.text: Hôtel du Tilleul, bonjour! Claire à l'appareil.
examples.trans: Hotel du Tilleul, good morning! Claire speaking.
Everything is going well.

examples.text: Madame Odette, tout va bien? Vous avez sonné!
examples.trans: Madam Odette, is everything alright? You rang the bell!
She's thirty.
Thirty euros, please.
Three weeks.
Three coffees.

meanings.note: ne fais pas cette tête = don't look like that; faire la tête = to sulk

meanings.en: c'est dans ma tête = it's all in my head

examples.trans: I have a headache.

examples.text: Pourquoi mes lunettes seraient... oh! Elles sont sur ma tête!
examples.trans: Why would my glasses be... oh! They are on my head!

meanings.note: indefinite article; des in the plural
Number; l'un = one of them.

examples.text: Et voilà la cloche du portail. Un coup franc.
examples.trans: There goes the gate bell. One firm ring.

examples.text: Voilà un taxi devant le portail à l'instant.
examples.trans: Here comes a taxi in front of the gate right now.

meanings.note: venir de + infinitive: je viens d'arriver = I've just arrived

meanings.en: venir de + infinitive = to have just
meanings.note: Je viens d'arriver.

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
examples.trans: I can't come tonight.
Are you coming?

related.word: venir de + infinitive: je viens d'arriver

meanings.note: Direction. Core French preposition meaning 'towards', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Time: vers midi. Core French preposition meaning 'towards', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.trans: A foot towards the grave.
We'll arrive around noon.

examples.text: J'ai senti un pied glisser vers la tombe.
examples.trans: I felt one foot slip towards the grave.

meanings.note: Dans la poche de votre veste = in your jacket pocket.

examples.text: Vos lunettes sont rangées dans la poche de votre veste.
examples.trans: Your glasses are tucked in your jacket pocket.

examples.text: Il boutonne sa veste propre avant d'aller au portail.
examples.trans: He buttons his clean jacket before going to the gate.

meanings.note: to present something or someone near you

examples.text: C'est vrai! Et voici les clés?
examples.trans: Fair enough! And here are the keys?

examples.text: Voici votre clé, numéro quatre. Le petit-déjeuner est de sept heures trente à dix heures.
examples.trans: Here is your key, number four. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

examples.text: Voici cinquante euros de la caisse. Rapportez le ticket!
examples.trans: Here is fifty euros from the cash box. Bring back the receipt!

meanings.note: masculine: voisin; feminine: voisine

examples.trans: What if she's your neighbour?
Our neighbours are nice.

meanings.note: One person, formal.
Several people.
je vous rappelle = I'll call you back

examples.trans: Where are you?

examples.text: Madame Odette, tout va bien? Vous avez sonné!
examples.trans: Madam Odette, is everything alright? You rang the bell!
I'm going there.
There are two seats.

meanings.note: Fragrant colored outer peel of an orange or lemon ('zeste d'orange', 'zeste de citron').

examples.text: Une pincée de zeste d'orange douce parfume merveilleusement le miel chaud.
examples.trans: A pinch of sweet orange zest scents the warm honey wonderfully.

examples.text: Elle ajoute un peu de zeste de citron râpé dans la pâte.
examples.trans: She adds a bit of grated lemon zest to the batter.

meanings.note: Place: à Paris, à mon cours.
Time: à midi.

meanings.en: au = à + le, aux = à + les
meanings.note: Contractions.

examples.trans: I'm in Paris.
At two pm.

meanings.note: Informal for cela.
With time.

examples.trans: I'll take that.
It's been three weeks.

meanings.note: No preposition.

meanings.en: écoute = listen, look (to start a point)
meanings.note: Casual imperative.

examples.trans: Listen, it's difficult.
I'm listening to the radio.

meanings.note: irregular verb; past participle: écrit

examples.text: Il veut écrire, diriger, choisir ses partenaires.
examples.trans: He wants to write, direct, choose his partners.
She is writing a new script.

meanings.note: The most common verb.
Ce + est.

examples.trans: I'm in Paris.
It's important.

meanings.note: Irregular plural: les yeux.

examples.text: Les yeux il y a deux ans.
examples.trans: Her eyes two years ago.
She has blue eyes.
